questions.question: I'm buying — compare Milford and Takapuna Central on zoning capacity and flood exposure.

quality.note: Thorough, accurate, keeps hazard layers separate, cites everything with the correct caveat and avoids collapsing into a single risk score, though slightly long.

anthropic.answer:
Milford spans three statistical areas, each with its own figures, so no single number covers the whole suburb. On **zoning/intensification capacity** (weighted more heavily in Buying mode), Takapuna Central leads at 52.7% {{c20}}, ahead of Milford Central at 39.3% {{c8}}, Westlake at 36.9% {{c14}}, and Milford West at just 10.3% {{c2}}. Consenting rates (also weighted heavily) tell a different story: Westlake is the most active at 37.1/1k dwellings {{c15}}, Milford Central at 30.8/1k {{c9}}, while Takapuna Central is quieter at 10.9/1k {{c21}} and Milford West at 13.7/1k {{c3}}.

On **flood exposure** (weighted heavily in Buying mode), Takapuna Central carries a notably high 1% AEP flood plain share of 49.11% {{c19}}, though its coastal inundation figures are relatively modest at 0.85% {{c24}} and 2.09% with +1m sea level rise {{c23}}, and its overland flow path density is the lowest of the group at 8.18 km/km² {{c22}}. Within Milford, flood plain exposure is meaningful across all three areas — Milford West at 23.67% {{c1}}, Westlake at 19.92% {{c13}}, Milford Central at 13.71% {{c7}} — with higher coastal inundation in Milford Central (7.91% {{c12}}, rising to 12.64% with sea level rise {{c11}}) and Milford West (4.89% {{c6}}, 6.92% {{c5}}); Westlake shows 0% coastal inundation on both measures {{c17}}{{c18}}.

In summary: Takapuna Central offers the highest intensification capacity but also the highest riverine flood plain share; within Milford, Westlake and Milford Central offer strong capacity with Westlake having no coastal inundation exposure, while Milford West lags on both zoning and consenting.
